First find A and B: let y=0, then -(x+1)^2+4=0, obtaining (x+1)^2=4, so x=1 or x=-3, therefore A=(-3,0), B=(1,0), and thus AB=4. Let P=(x,y) be on the parabola. Substitute AB=4, obtaining 1/2 × 4 × |y| = 8, so |y|=4. Thus it only needs to be solved simultaneously with the parabola for y=4 and y=-4. 1) When y=4, -(x+1)^2+4=4, obtaining (x+1)^2=0, hence x=-1, P=(-1,4). 2) When y=-4, -(x+1)^2+4=-4, obtaining (x+1)^2=8, hence x=-1±2\sqrt{2}, corresponding to P=(-1+2\sqrt{2},-4) and P=(-1-2\sqrt{2},-4). So such points P exist, with three in total.

Thus it only needs to be solved simultaneously with the parabola for y=4 and y=-4.
1) When y=4, -(x+1)^2+4=4, obtaining (x+1)^2=0, hence x=-1, P=(-1,4).
2) When y=-4, -(x+1)^2+4=-4, obtaining (x+1)^2=8, hence x=-1±2\sqrt{2}, corresponding to P=(-1+2\sqrt{2},-4) and P=(-1-2\sqrt{2},-4).

So such points P exist, with three in total.
